# Independent audit: common-interior projected counting obstruction

Audited source:
`candidate 74ee0d47d99d3779`.


1. The determinant of E=conv(0,(1/3+epsilon,1/3),
   (1/3,1/3+epsilon)) is epsilon(2/3+epsilon). Its nonzero vertices
   are in T, so E subset T. The Cayley hull has N exact T fibers and
   one exact E fiber at the integer bases. On the last real interval
   its slice is (N-z)T+(z-N+1)E: any representation using an earlier
   T level puts a larger weight on E and hence gives a subset, because
   E subset T. Every real fiber contains E.

2. The stated two non-apex E barycentric weights of p are equal,
   positive, and sum to less than one. The missing apex weight is
   (epsilon+2theta)/(2/3+epsilon)>0. Thus p is strictly interior even
   to the smallest fiber, with no supporting-facet exception.

3. I recomputed all cap areas by independent exact polygon clipping.
   H_0 cuts a similar apex triangle in E; H_1 and H_2 have complementary
   apex triangles with different edge ratios. This confirms both
   formulas (1), including their proper-cut ranges and zero-area
   boundaries. The thresholds sum to one and their three boundaries
   pass through p, so the caps really cover all of R^2. Their individual
   upper masses therefore bound ordinary maximal depth at every point.

4. The budget estimates are exact. The large-triangle contributions
   add e/3+e theta/4 for H_1,H_2, while the E fraction is at most
   3epsilon+6theta. This gives the coefficient 25theta/4. The inequality
   theta<=epsilon/16 yields 3epsilon+25theta/4<=217/6400, and
   4/9-1/3-217/6400=4447/57600>0. For H_0 the corresponding excess is
   at most e(1/3+theta), which satisfies the same displayed common bound.

5. The lower bounds keep ordinary projection and mixed depth separate.
   N copies of T pay N Gamma in any projected through-g direction.
   For odd N=2k+1, the actual point (k,g) has at least k+1 whole fiber
   indices on the favorable side of every base tilt. Each trace then
   contains the ordinary through-g cap of T. Vertical caps include
   their boundary fiber and also satisfy the bound. Since e<1, the
   resulting normalized mixed lower bound is strictly above Gamma/2.

6. The scope is correct: this disproves a universal projected Gamma_2
   bound even with a common affine interior section and arbitrarily
   many actual positive fibers. It neither identifies the exact
   projected maximum nor disproves the mixed Gamma_2/2 target.

Verification: the supplied verifier passes all 462 checks. The independent
`supporting computation verify_common_interior_projected_count_functional_audit.py` also passes;
it clips the two actual triangles directly with rational arithmetic,
rather than only checking the asserted area expressions against bounds.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
